notes:
Short summary / CRM-style bullets:
- Primary workload: low-latency conversational routing for driver dispatch + reranking for candidate routes; embeddings for similarity search of historical routes.
- Latency targets: p95 < 120ms, p99 goal < 200ms for 256-token chat sessions; throughputs: sustained 400-600 rps during peak, spike bursts to 1.5k rps for <10m windows.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high — will trade predictable reserved cost for lower unit price; procurement prefers committed capacity + clear autoscaling rules.
- Model preference: community Llama-3 variants (quant-friendly), open to Redwood-verified variants with per-model profiles.
- Routing/fallback: must automatically fallback to smaller model family on capacity constraints; need tiered fallback policy (dedicated -> shared-hosted) with request-level routing.
- Security: VPC-private control plane, SSO/SAML + SCIM, KMS integration (customer-managed keys), audit logs 1 year retention, EU data residency for EU customers.
- Autoscaling notes from SE: prefer warm-pool approach (maintain 2 pre-warmed instances per AZ), aggressive scale-up (cpu/gpu queue > 60% or queue latency > 50ms) with cooldown 30s; conservative scale-down (idle > 10m) to avoid cold starts impacting p99.
- Queueing behavior: propose bounded request queue with per-tenant TTL 5s and circuit-breaker for backpressure; spike queueing should be handled by burst nodes + short-term token-bucket smoothing.
- Warm pool specifics discussed: pre-pull kernels and KV caches for top-4 model variants; cost delta estimated ~12% of reserved spend but reduces p99 by ~80ms in tests.
- POC issues: observed p99 spikes at steady-state due to GC and kernel JIT on first warmups; mitigation tested via pre-warm scripts and pinned quant kernels.
- AE notes: "They care about predictable latency more than absolute lowest cost; procurement will push back on burst pricing unless capped."
- SE notes: "Need final sign-off on A/B fallback policy and canary rollouts; recommend 2-week canary with synthetic traffic before cutover."
